beats.line: Hola. This is Liam, in for Bear. Everyone wants one AI — one subscription, one app, done. So which is it: ChatGPT or Claude? I typed that exact question into Claude. Here’s what came back — and the part it got right.
beats.screen: Composer sketch: window, 'Hola, Liam', typed question, three answer lines fade in.

beats.line: Here’s the whole film in one breath. Stop shopping for the smartest AI on a leaderboard. The question isn’t which one is best on a chart — it’s which one fits the work you actually do. And the only honest test is running your own real tasks through it. That’s the film. Now the details.
beats.screen: Writer types 'The question isn't which is smartest.' — 'smartest' struck, replaced by 'best on a chart'.

beats.line: Four words you’ll hear, in plain English. A model: the AI engine under the hood — you never see it directly. A prompt: what you type into the chat box. Context: what the AI already knows about you when a chat starts. And a benchmark: a test score on a chart. Useful for labs. Not for you.
beats.screen: Four term cards land one by one: model / prompt / context / benchmark.

beats.line: The one rule, before anything else. If your company pays for one of these, use it properly — learn the thing you’re already paying for instead of shopping for a better one. If you can afford both, get both. That’s not a dodge. It’s the honest answer. And the real benchmark isn’t a chart online — it’s your own work, run through the thing.
beats.screen: Two doors: 'the one you have' / 'both'; a bar-chart card gets a red X.

beats.line: Why not the chart? Because a benchmark measures what the lab wanted measured — tidy test questions with right answers. Your job isn’t a tidy test question. The chart tells you which engine is fastest on a track. It can’t tell you which car fits your driveway.
beats.screen: Leaderboard bars with trophy get a big red X; a car settles into a driveway.

beats.line: Here’s why Claude makes a default work brain, and it’s boring: it remembers. You keep a folder of files — who you are, what your company does, how you like things written — and Claude reads them at the start of every session. No more retyping your background in every chat. One folder, written once, beats a hundred clever prompts you saved and never used.
beats.screen: Left: chat window, same background line retyped 3x. Right: folder of 3 files feeds the session once.

beats.line: Meanwhile ChatGPT earned its tab back. Describe an image change in plain words and it edits the picture, right in the chat. It opens your spreadsheets and documents and works on them with you, no switching apps. And when a question needs real digging, its search goes deeper. Three jobs where it’s genuinely the better pick.
beats.screen: Three tiles land: image with edit arrow, spreadsheet grid, magnifier.

beats.line: Two shortcuts, if you want the decision made for you. If most of your job is writing — reports, briefs, emails, anything long — start with Claude and its memory folder. If your week lives in images, spreadsheets, and deep research — start with ChatGPT. Those are the two exits. Pick one, and then test it.
beats.screen: Two columns, held: writing -> Claude (+ memory folder) / images, sheets, research -> ChatGPT.

beats.line: The test takes thirty minutes, not thirty days. One real task from your week. Run it in both — same task, same afternoon. Put the two answers side by side and compare. Whichever one earned the tab, that’s your answer. Charts measure what labs want measured. You measure what you need.
beats.screen: Stopwatch '30:00'; two output cards side by side; green check lands on one.

beats.line: So the verdict. One AI is a fantasy — the stack is the answer. Claude for the long-form work, kept sharp by a folder of context you write once. ChatGPT for images, spreadsheets, and deep search. There are specialists beyond those two, and they’re fine. But nothing outranks the test: your work, your tasks, your judgment. If the test ever says the chart was right, believe the chart — but run the test first.
beats.screen: Four verdict lines with dot bullets, revealed one by one.

beats.line: Your turn. Paste this into Claude: ‘Interview me about my work week — my writing, my spreadsheets, my images — then tell me which AI should be my default, and name one task I should test in both this week.’ Answer it honestly and see what it prescribes. Then run the test it suggests. That’s this whole film, applied to you.
beats.screen: Prompt card: the paste-into-Claude interview prompt.

beats.line: ChatGPT or Claude? Liam, in for Bear. Thanks for watching.
